title: Home Automation — Final Recap 🏆
description: An overall review of the whole ESP32 home automation build.

questions.prompt: The pattern behind every home automation project is:
questions.explanation: Read the world, decide, act. The DHT22, ESP32, and RGB LED are those three steps.

questions.prompt: Match the roles: in our build, the sensor / brain / output were...
questions.explanation: DHT22 reads, ESP32 thinks, RGB LED shows the result.

questions.prompt: Which pin controlled which part? Pick the correct set.
questions.explanation: DATA on GPIO 4, and the RGB channels on 18 (R), 19 (G), 23 (B).

questions.prompt: Why does the DHT22 need that 10 kΩ pull-up resistor?
choices: The bare sensor has no built-in pull-up, so it keeps the DATA line clean
questions.explanation: No pull-up → garbled reads (NaN). It holds the data line HIGH between pulses.

questions.prompt: On the RGB LED, the longest leg is the common cathode. It connects to...
questions.explanation: Common cathode = shared negative leg → straight to GND, no resistor on that leg.

questions.prompt: PWM (Pulse-Width Modulation) lets us control the LED by...
choices: Blinking it faster than the eye can see to fake different brightness
questions.explanation: Fast on/off pulses average out to look like dimmer or brighter light.

questions.prompt: In humidity mode, order the colors from driest to most humid:
setup() vs loop(): which is right?
choices: setup() runs once at startup; loop() runs forever
setup() runs forever; loop() runs once
Neither runs unless you press a button
questions.explanation: Initialize in setup(), then repeat your main work in loop().

questions.prompt: If dht.readHumidity() returns NaN, the best first thing to check is:
choices: The wiring and the pull-up resistor
Whether the room is too quiet
questions.explanation: NaN almost always means a loose/missing wire, wrong pin, or missing pull-up.

questions.prompt: You're powered up and about to move a wire to a new pin. What should you do first?
choices: Unplug the USB cable so the board isn't powered
Nothing — rewire while it's on to save time
questions.explanation: Always unplug before rewiring — never change a circuit while it's powered.
